q: Out of the following four sentences, select the most suitable sentence with respect to grammar and usage.
opts: I will not leave the place until the minister does not meet me.
I will not leave the place until the minister doesn't meet me.
I will not leave the place until the minister meet me.
I will not leave the place until the minister meets me.
exp:
'Until' khud mein negative sense rakhta hai (= jab tak nahi).
Isliye 'until ... does not' double negative ban jata hai -> A, B galat.
Subject 'the minister' singular hai, to verb 'meets' chahiye -> C galat.
D: 'until the minister meets me' grammatically sahi.
Trap: Hindi ke 'jab tak nahi milte' ko direct translate karke 'does not' lagana.
Answer: D

q: A rewording of something written or spoken is a ______________.
exp:
Paraphrase = kisi baat ko apne words mein dobara kehna (rewording).
Paradox = self-contradictory statement.
Paradigm = model / pattern.
Paraffin = ek wax / fuel.
Answer: A (paraphrase)

q:
Archimedes said, "Give me a lever long enough and a fulcrum on which to place it, and I will move the world."
The sentence above is an example of a ___________ statement.
exp:
Archimedes literally duniya hilane ki baat nahi kar rahe, lever ki power ko exaggerate karke bata rahe hain.
Aisa non-literal, symbolic language = figurative statement.
Literal ka matlab exact word-by-word meaning - yahan nahi.
Figurine = chhoti murti, collateral = security/side - irrelevant.
Answer: A

q: If 'relftaga' means carefree, 'otaga' means careful and 'fertaga' means careless, which of the following could mean 'aftercare'?
exp:
Teeno words mein common 'taga' = care.
Pattern: suffix ka code pehle aata hai, 'taga' baad mein: relf+taga = care+free, o+taga = care+ful, fer+taga = care+less.
Yani English mein jo word 'care' ke baad aata hai, code mein woh pehle aata hai.
'aftercare' mein 'after' care se PEHLE hai, to code mein 'after' ka code taga ke BAAD aayega: taga + (new code).
Options mein tagazen fit hota hai (zen = after, naya code); tagafer = care-less hoga.
Answer: C

q: A cube is built using 64 cubic blocks of side one unit. After it is built, one cubic block is removed from every corner of the cube. The resulting surface area of the body (in square units) after the removal is __________.
exp:
64 blocks -> cube ki side 4. Original surface area = 6 x 4² = 96.
Ek corner block hatane par uske 3 exposed faces chale jaate hain (-3).
Lekin andar ke 3 naye faces expose ho jaate hain (+3).
Net change = 0 har corner ke liye.
Isliye surface area 96 hi rehta hai.
Trap: 8 x 3 = 24 minus karke 72 choose karna.
Answer: D (96)

q:
A shaving set company sells 4 different types of razors, Elegance, Smooth, Soft and Executive. Elegance sells at Rs. 48, Smooth at Rs. 63, Soft at Rs. 78 and Executive at Rs. 173 per piece. The table below shows the numbers of each razor sold in each quarter of a year.

Quarter \ Product | Elegance | Smooth | Soft  | Executive
Q1                | 27300    | 20009  | 17602 | 9999
Q2                | 25222    | 19392  | 18445 | 8942
Q3                | 28976    | 22429  | 19544 | 10234
Q4                | 21012    | 18229  | 16595 | 10109

Which product contributes the greatest fraction to the revenue of the company in that year?
exp:
Har product ki yearly units x price nikaalo.
Elegance: 27300+25222+28976+21012 = 102510 x 48 = 49,20,480
Smooth: 80059 x 63 = 50,43,717
Soft: 72186 x 78 = 56,30,508
Executive: 9999+8942+10234+10109 = 39284 x 173 = 67,96,132
Sabse zyada revenue Executive ka.
Trap: sirf units dekh kar Elegance choose karna.
Answer: B

q:
Indian currency notes show the denomination indicated in at least seventeen languages. If this is not an indication of the nation's diversity, nothing else is.
Which of the following can be logically inferred from the above sentences?
opts: India is a country of exactly seventeen languages.
Linguistic pluralism is the only indicator of a nation's diversity.
Indian currency notes have sufficient space for all the Indian languages.
Linguistic pluralism is strong evidence of India's diversity.
exp:
Passage 'at least seventeen' kehta hai, 'exactly' nahi -> A galat.
'If this is not an indication..., nothing else is' ek strong emphasis hai, 'only indicator' claim nahi -> B zyada strong.
Notes ki space ke baare mein kuch nahi kaha -> C galat.
Author bol raha hai ki languages ki variety diversity ka strong proof hai.
Answer: D

q:
Consider the following statements relating to the level of poker play of four players P, Q, R and S.
I. P always beats Q
II. R always beats S
III. S loses to P only sometimes
IV. R always loses to Q
Which of the following can be logically inferred from the above statements?
(i) P is likely to beat all the three other players
(ii) S is the absolute worst player in the set
exp:
Chain: P > Q > R > S (always beats) lagta hai.
Lekin III: S P se 'only sometimes' haarta hai, yani S aksar P ko hara deta hai.
Toh P sabko beat karega yeh nahi keh sakte -> (i) infer nahi hota.
S, P ko often beat karta hai, to S 'absolute worst' bhi nahi kaha ja sakta -> (ii) bhi nahi.
Poker mein transitivity guaranteed nahi hai.
Answer: D

q: If f(x) = 2x⁷ + 3x − 5, which of the following is a factor of f(x)?
exp:
Factor theorem: (x − a) factor hai agar f(a) = 0.
f(1) = 2 + 3 − 5 = 0 -> (x − 1) factor hai.
Check: f(−1) = −2 − 3 − 5 = −10 ≠ 0.
f(5/2) bahut bada positive, 0 nahi.
x³+8 ka root x = −2: f(−2) = −256 − 6 − 5 ≠ 0.
Answer: B

q: In a process, the number of cycles to failure decreases exponentially with an increase in load. At a load of 80 units, it takes 100 cycles for failure. When the load is halved, it takes 10000 cycles for failure. The load for which the failure will happen in 5000 cycles is ________.

Let p, q, r, s represent the following propositions.
p: x ∈ {8, 9, 10, 11, 12}
q: x is a composite number
r: x is a perfect square
s: x is a prime number
The integer x ≥ 2 which satisfies ¬((p ⇒ q) ∧ (¬r ∨ ¬s)) is ________.
exp:
¬((p⇒q) ∧ (¬r∨¬s)) = ¬(p⇒q) ∨ ¬(¬r∨¬s) = (p ∧ ¬q) ∨ (r ∧ s).
r ∧ s: perfect square AND prime - koi number aisa nahi, so false.
Toh chahiye p ∧ ¬q: x ∈ {8,...,12} aur x composite NAHI.
8, 9, 10, 12 composite hain; sirf 11 prime (non-composite).
Answer: 11

q: Let aₙ be the number of n-bit strings that do NOT contain two consecutive 1s. Which one of the following is the recurrence relation for aₙ?
exp:
Valid string ka last bit dekho.
Agar last bit 0 hai: pehle ke n−1 bits koi bhi valid string -> aₙ₋₁ ways.
Agar last bit 1 hai: uske pehle 0 hona zaroori ('01' end) -> pehle n−2 bits valid -> aₙ₋₂ ways.
aₙ = aₙ₋₁ + aₙ₋₂ (Fibonacci type).
Check: a₁=2, a₂=3, a₃=5 ✓.
Answer: B

Put t = x − 4, x→4 matlab t→0.
Limit = lim (t→0) sin t / t.
Standard limit: sin t / t → 1.
Answer: 1

q: A probability density function on the interval [a, 1] is given by 1/x² and outside this interval the value of the function is zero. The value of a is ________.
exp:
PDF ka total area 1 hona chahiye.
∫ₐ¹ (1/x²) dx = [−1/x]ₐ¹ = −1 + 1/a.
1/a − 1 = 1 -> 1/a = 2 -> a = 0.5.
Answer: 0.5

q: Two eigenvalues of a 3 × 3 real matrix P are (2 + √−1) and 3. The determinant of P is ________.
exp:
Real matrix ke complex eigenvalues conjugate pairs mein aate hain.
Toh 2 + i hai to 2 − i bhi eigenvalue hai.
Teeno eigenvalues: 2+i, 2−i, 3.
det P = product = (2+i)(2−i) × 3 = (4+1) × 3 = 15.
Answer: 15

q:
Consider the Boolean operator # with the following properties:
x # 0 = x, x # 1 = x', x # x = 0 and x # x' = 1. Then x # y is equivalent to
exp:
Properties dekho: x#0 = x, x#1 = x', x#x = 0, x#x' = 1.
Yeh exactly XOR ke properties hain.
x ⊕ y = xy' + x'y.
Check: y=0 -> x ✓, y=1 -> x' ✓.
Answer: A

q: The 16-bit 2's complement representation of an integer is 1111 1111 1111 0101; its decimal representation is ________.
exp:
MSB = 1 -> negative number.
Magnitude = 2's complement lo: invert -> 0000 0000 0000 1010, +1 -> 0000 0000 0000 1011 = 11.
Toh number = −11.
Answer: −11

q: We want to design a synchronous counter that counts the sequence 0-1-0-2-0-3 and then repeats. The minimum number of J-K flip-flops required to implement this counter is ________.
exp:
Sequence mein 0 teen baar aata hai, lekin har 0 ke baad next state alag hai (1, 2, 3).
Toh har 0 ko alag state maanna padega -> total 6 distinct states.
Minimum flip-flops = ⌈log₂ 6⌉ = 3 (output decode karne ke liye combinational logic).
Official key 3 se 4 tak range accept karti hai (extra flip-flop use karke design bhi possible).
Trap: sirf 4 distinct values (0,1,2,3) dekh kar 2 bolna.
Answer: 3 (range 3–4)

q: A processor can support a maximum memory of 4 GB, where the memory is word-addressable (a word consists of two bytes). The size of the address bus of the processor is at least ________ bits.
exp:
Memory = 4 GB = 2³² bytes.
Word = 2 bytes, word-addressable -> number of words = 2³² / 2 = 2³¹.
Har word ko unique address chahiye -> 31 address bits.
Trap: byte-addressable maan kar 32 bolna.
Answer: 31

q: A queue is implemented using an array such that ENQUEUE and DEQUEUE operations are performed efficiently. Which one of the following statements is CORRECT (n refers to the number of items in the queue)?
opts: Both operations can be performed in O(1) time
At most one operation can be performed in O(1) time but the worst case time for the other operation will be Ω(n)
The worst case time complexity for both operations will be Ω(n)
Worst case time complexity for both operations will be Ω(log n)
exp:
Array mein circular queue banao: front aur rear do indices.
ENQUEUE: rear = (rear+1) mod size, element daalo -> O(1).
DEQUEUE: front = (front+1) mod size -> O(1).
Koi shifting nahi karni padti.
Answer: A

q:
Consider the following directed graph:
Edges: a → b, b → c, c → f, a → d, d → e, e → f
The number of different topological orderings of the vertices of the graph is ________.
exp:
a ka indegree 0 -> a hamesha pehle; f sabse last.
Beech mein do independent chains: b→c aur d→e.
In 4 vertices ko interleave karna hai, har chain ka order fixed.
Ways = C(4,2) = 6.
Answer: 6

q:
Consider the following C program.
Which one of the following expressions, when placed in the blank above, will NOT result in a type checking error?
exp:
f(int, short) return type void hai.
A, C: *s -> s pointer nahi, short hai, dereference error.
B: i = f(i,s) -> void value ko int mein assign nahi kar sakte, error.
D: f(i, *p) -> i int, *p short (p short* hai) -> perfect match.
Answer: D

q: The worst case running times of Insertion sort, Merge sort and Quick sort, respectively, are:
opts: Θ(n log n), Θ(n log n), and Θ(n²)
Θ(n²), Θ(n²), and Θ(n log n)
Θ(n²), Θ(n log n), and Θ(n log n)
Θ(n²), Θ(n log n), and Θ(n²)
exp:
Insertion sort worst case (reverse sorted) -> Θ(n²).
Merge sort hamesha n log n -> Θ(n log n).
Quick sort worst case (bad pivot, e.g. sorted input with first-element pivot) -> Θ(n²).
Answer: D

q:
Let G be a weighted connected undirected graph with distinct positive edge weights. If every edge weight is increased by the same value, then which of the following statements is/are TRUE?
P: Minimum spanning tree of G does not change
Q: Shortest path between any pair of vertices does not change
exp:
MST sirf edges ke relative order par depend karta hai (Kruskal). Sabme same c add karne se order same -> MST same. P true.
Shortest path: path mein k edges hain to weight k·c badhta hai; zyada edges wala path zyada penalize hota hai.
Example: A–B direct 5, A–C–B = 2+2 = 4. Add 2: direct 7, via C 8 -> shortest path badal gaya.
Q false.
Answer: A

q:
Consider the following C program.
The output of the program is ________.
exp:
mystery() sirf local pointer copies ptra, ptrb ko swap karta hai.
C call-by-value hai - pointers ki copies swap hui, *ptra/*ptrb (actual values) touch nahi hue.
Toh a, b, c, d kabhi change nahi hote.
a=2016, c=4: (a < c) false, waise bhi koi effect nahi.
printf a -> 2016.
Trap: sochna ki swap ho gaya.
Answer: 2016

q:
Which of the following languages is generated by the given grammar?
S → aS | bS | ε
opts: {w ∈ {a, b}* | w has equal number of a's and b's}
exp:
Har step pe a ya b koi bhi add kar sakte ho, aur ε se khatam.
Toh a aur b ka koi bhi sequence, kisi bhi order mein -> {a,b}*.
Example: 'ba' generate hota hai (S→bS→baS→ba), jo A mein nahi hai.
Answer: D

q:
Which of the following decision problems are undecidable?
I. Given NFAs N₁ and N₂, is L(N₁) ∩ L(N₂) = Φ?
II. Given a CFG G = (N, Σ, P, S) and a string x ∈ Σ*, does x ∈ L(G)?
III. Given CFGs G₁ and G₂, is L(G₁) = L(G₂)?
IV. Given a TM M, is L(M) = Φ?
exp:
I: regular languages ka intersection regular, emptiness decidable -> decidable.
II: CFG membership -> CYK algorithm se decidable.
III: CFG equivalence -> undecidable.
IV: TM emptiness -> Rice's theorem se undecidable.
Answer: C (III and IV)

q: Which one of the following regular expressions represents the language: the set of all binary strings having two consecutive 0s and two consecutive 1s?
exp:
String mein '00' aur '11' dono hone chahiye, kisi bhi order mein, beech mein kuch bhi.
B: 00 pehle phir kabhi 11, ya 11 pehle phir kabhi 00, aage-peeche kuch bhi -> exact.
A: 00 aur 11 adjacent ('0011'/'1100') hone chahiye -> '00111'? nahi, '001011' jaisi valid string miss ho jaati hai.
C: '+' hai, to sirf ek bhi ho to accept -> galat.
D: string 00/11 se start aur end honi chahiye -> '0011x' type miss.
Answer: B

q:
Consider the following code segment.
The minimum number of total variables required to convert the above code segment to static single assignment form is ________.
exp:
SSA mein har variable ek hi baar assign hota hai.
x1 = u − t
y1 = x1 * v
x2 = y1 + w
y2 = t − z
y3 = x2 * y2
Naye variables: x1, x2, y1, y2, y3 = 5; original inputs u, t, v, w, z = 5.
Total = 10.
Trap: sirf naye 5 ginna.
Answer: 10

q: Consider an arbitrary set of CPU-bound processes with unequal CPU burst lengths submitted at the same time to a computer system. Which one of the following process scheduling algorithms would minimize the average waiting time in the ready queue?
opts: Round-robin with time quantum less than the shortest CPU burst
Highest priority first with priority proportional to CPU burst length
exp:
SJF/SRTF average waiting time ko provably minimize karta hai.
Sab ek saath aaye hain, to SRTF = SJF (preemption ki zarurat nahi).
Round robin se context switches aur waiting badhti hai.
D ulta hai - longest job first, sabse bura.
Answer: A

q: Which of the following is NOT a superkey in a relational schema with attributes V, W, X, Y, Z and primary key VY?
exp:
Superkey = koi bhi attribute set jo primary key VY ko contain kare.
A: VXYZ -> V, Y dono hain ✓.
B: VWXZ -> Y missing ✗.
C: VWXY ✓, D: VWXYZ ✓.
Answer: B

q: Which one of the following is NOT a part of the ACID properties of database transactions?
exp:
ACID = Atomicity, Consistency, Isolation, Durability.
Deadlock-freedom ACID ka part nahi hai.
Answer: D

q:
A database of research articles in a journal uses the following schema.
(VOLUME, NUMBER, STARTPAGE, ENDPAGE, TITLE, YEAR, PRICE)
The primary key is (VOLUME, NUMBER, STARTPAGE, ENDPAGE) and the following functional dependencies exist in the schema.
(VOLUME, NUMBER, STARTPAGE, ENDPAGE) → TITLE
(VOLUME, NUMBER) → YEAR
(VOLUME, NUMBER, STARTPAGE, ENDPAGE) → PRICE
The database is redesigned to use the following schemas.
(VOLUME, NUMBER, STARTPAGE, ENDPAGE, TITLE, PRICE)
(VOLUME, NUMBER, YEAR)
Which is the weakest normal form that the new database satisfies, but the old one does not?
exp:
Old schema: (VOLUME, NUMBER) → YEAR, jahan (VOLUME, NUMBER) key ka proper subset hai.
Non-prime YEAR partially dependent -> 2NF violate. Old = sirf 1NF.
New schema: dono tables mein har FD ka LHS key hai -> BCNF tak satisfy.
New jo satisfy karta hai par old nahi: 2NF, 3NF, BCNF - inme weakest = 2NF.
Answer: B

q: Which one of the following protocols is NOT used to resolve one form of address to another one?
exp:
DNS: hostname -> IP address.
ARP: IP -> MAC.
RARP: MAC -> IP.
DHCP: IP address dynamically assign/allocate karta hai, resolution nahi.
Answer: C

q:
Which of the following is/are example(s) of stateful application layer protocols?
(i) HTTP
(ii) FTP
(iii) TCP
(iv) POP3
exp:
HTTP stateless hai (har request independent).
TCP transport layer ka hai, application layer nahi.
FTP session state rakhta hai (current directory, login).
POP3 bhi session state rakhta hai (authorization/transaction states).
Answer: C

q: The coefficient of x¹² in (x³ + x⁴ + x⁵ + x⁶ + ···)³ is ________.
exp:
(x³ + x⁴ + ...)³ = x⁹ (1 + x + x² + ...)³ = x⁹ / (1 − x)³.
x¹² ka coefficient = (1−x)⁻³ mein x³ ka coefficient.
(1−x)⁻³ mein xᵏ ka coefficient = C(k+2, 2).
k=3: C(5,2) = 10.
Answer: 10

q: Consider the recurrence relation a₁ = 8, aₙ = 6n² + 2n + aₙ₋₁. Let a₉₉ = K × 10⁴. The value of K is ________.

A function f : N⁺ → N⁺, defined on the set of positive integers N⁺, satisfies the following properties:
f(n) = f(n/2) if n is even
f(n) = f(n + 5) if n is odd
Let R = {i | ∃j : f(j) = i} be the set of distinct values that f takes. The maximum possible size of R is ________.
exp:
Dekho kaunse numbers ek hi value par forced hain.
f(1)=f(6)=f(3)=f(8)=f(4)=f(2)=f(1) -> 1,2,3,4,6,8 same class. f(7)=f(12)=f(6), f(9)=f(14)=f(7) -> sab non-multiples of 5 ek class mein.
Multiples of 5: f(5)=f(10)=f(5), f(15)=f(20)=f(10) -> sab ek alag class.
Odd n ke liye n+5 aur even ke liye n/2 - dono operations 5-divisibility preserve karte hain, isliye do classes kabhi merge nahi hoti.
Toh f maximum 2 distinct values le sakta hai.
Answer: 2

q:
Consider the following experiment.
Step 1. Flip a fair coin twice.
Step 2. If the outcomes are (TAILS, HEADS) then output Y and stop.
Step 3. If the outcomes are either (HEADS, HEADS) or (HEADS, TAILS), then output N and stop.
Step 4. If the outcomes are (TAILS, TAILS), then go to Step 1.
The probability that the output of the experiment is Y is (up to two decimal places) ________.
exp:
Ek round mein: P(TH) = 1/4 -> Y, P(HH or HT) = 1/2 -> N, P(TT) = 1/4 -> repeat.
P(Y) = 1/4 + (1/4)·P(Y) -> P(Y)(3/4) = 1/4.
P(Y) = 1/3 ≈ 0.33.
Shortcut: repeat ignore karo, terminating outcomes mein Y ka share = (1/4)/(3/4).
Answer: 0.33

q:
Consider the two cascaded 2-to-1 multiplexers as shown in the figure.
MUX1: input 0 = 0, input 1 = R, select s = P; its output goes to input 1 of MUX2.
MUX2: input 0 = R', input 1 = output of MUX1, select s = Q; output = X.
The minimal sum of products form of the output X is
exp:
MUX1 output = P'·0 + P·R = PR.
MUX2 output X = Q'·(R') + Q·(PR).
X = Q'R' + PQR.
Yeh already minimal hai (koi common term combine nahi hota).
Answer: D

q: The size of the data count register of a DMA controller is 16 bits. The processor needs to transfer a file of 29,154 kilobytes from disk to main memory. The memory is byte addressable. The minimum number of times the DMA controller needs to get the control of the system bus from the processor to transfer the file from the disk to main memory is ________.
exp:
16-bit count register -> ek baar mein max 2¹⁶ bytes = 64 KB transfer.
File = 29154 KB.
Bus kitni baar chahiye = ⌈29154 / 64⌉ = ⌈455.53⌉ = 456.
Answer: 456

q: The stage delays in a 4-stage pipeline are 800, 500, 400 and 300 picoseconds. The first stage (with delay 800 picoseconds) is replaced with a functionally equivalent design involving two stages with respective delays 600 and 350 picoseconds. The throughput increase of the pipeline is ________ percent.
exp:
Pipeline cycle time = max stage delay.
Old: max(800,500,400,300) = 800 ps -> throughput 1/800.
New stages: 600, 350, 500, 400, 300 -> cycle = 600 ps -> throughput 1/600.
Increase = (1/600 − 1/800)/(1/800) = 800/600 − 1 = 33.33%.
Answer: ≈ 33.33

q: Consider a carry lookahead adder for adding two n-bit integers, built using gates of fan-in at most two. The time to perform addition using this adder is
exp:
CLA mein carry cᵢ ke liye i+1 terms ka AND/OR chahiye.
Unlimited fan-in ho to constant depth, lekin fan-in ≤ 2 hai.
n inputs ka AND/OR fan-in 2 gates se binary tree banta hai -> depth Θ(log n).
Toh addition time Θ(log n).
Answer: B

The following function computes the maximum value contained in an integer array p[] of size n (n >= 1).
The missing loop condition is
exp:

q: What will be the output of the following C program?
exp:
d static hai -> sab calls mein ek hi copy, sirf ek baar 1 se initialize.
count(3): print 3, 1; d=2; call count(2).
count(2): print 2, 2; d=3; call count(1).
count(1): print 1, 3; d=4; n>1 false; print 4.
Return count(2): print 4. Return count(3): print 4.
Output: 3 1 2 2 1 3 4 4 4.

q: What will be the output of the following pseudo-code when parameters are passed by reference and dynamic scoping is assumed?
exp:
Official key: D (4, 4). Intended trace:
main m(a) call karta hai; y ko a ki value 3 milti hai (key isi reading par based hai).
m mein: a = 1; a = y − a = 3 − 1 = 2.
n(a): x reference hai a ka; dynamic scoping se n ke andar a = global a = 2.

q: An operator delete(i) for a binary heap data structure is to be designed to delete the item in the i-th node. Assume that the heap is implemented in an array and i refers to the i-th index of the array. If the heap tree has depth d (number of edges on the path from the root to the farthest leaf), then what is the time complexity to re-fix the heap efficiently after the removal of the element?
exp:
i-th element ko last element se replace karo, size ek kam karo.
Ab naya element ya to upar jaayega (heapify-up) ya neeche (heapify-down) - ek hi direction.
Dono mein maximum path length = d -> O(d).
Worst case (e.g. root delete) mein d steps lagte hain, isliye O(1) nahi.
Answer: B

q:
Consider the weighted undirected graph with 4 vertices, where the weight of edge {i, j} is given by the entry Wᵢⱼ in the matrix W.
W =
[0 2 8 5]
[2 0 5 8]
[8 5 0 x]
[5 8 x 0]
The largest possible integer value of x, for which at least one shortest path between some pair of vertices will contain the edge with weight x is ________.
exp:
Vertices 1,2,3,4. Edge x = {3,4}. Edge x kisi shortest path mein tabhi hoga jab 3–4 ka direct edge ≤ baaki raaston ke.
3 se 4 ke alternate paths: 3–1–4 = 8+5 = 13, 3–2–4 = 5+8 = 13, 3–2–1–4 = 5+2+5 = 12.
Sabse chhota alternate = 12.
x = 12 par direct edge bhi ek shortest path hai (tie) -> 'at least one shortest path' satisfy.
x = 13 par 3–2–1–4 (12) better, aur kisi aur pair ke liye bhi x use nahi hoga.
Answer: 12

q: Let G be a complete undirected graph on 4 vertices, having 6 edges with weights being 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, and 6. The maximum possible weight that a minimum weight spanning tree of G can have is ________.
exp:
MST mein 3 edges. Kruskal: edge 1 aur 2 hamesha liye jayenge (2 edges cycle nahi bana sakte).
MST weight maximize karna hai: edge 3 ko reject karwao -> 1, 2, 3 ek triangle bana do.
Triangle ke 3 vertices ke baad 4th vertex ko jodne wale edges 4, 5, 6 hain; sabse chhota 4 MST mein aayega.
MST = 1 + 2 + 4 = 7.
Edge 4 ko bhi reject karna possible nahi (4th vertex ko connect karna hi hai, aur 4,5,6 hi bache hain).
Answer: 7

q:
G = (V, E) is an undirected simple graph in which each edge has a distinct weight, and e is a particular edge of G. Which of the following statements about the minimum spanning trees (MSTs) of G is/are TRUE?
I. If e is the lightest edge of some cycle in G, then every MST of G includes e
II. If e is the heaviest edge of some cycle in G, then every MST of G excludes e
exp:
II: Cycle property - distinct weights mein kisi cycle ka heaviest edge kabhi MST mein nahi hota. True.
I: False. Counterexample: edges AB=3, AC=1, CB=2, AD=4, DB=5.
Cycle A–B–D (3,5,4) mein AB lightest hai, lekin cycle A–C–B (1,2,3) mein AB heaviest hai -> MST se exclude.
Lightest edge of some cycle hona MST mein aane ki guarantee nahi (cut property chahiye, cycle nahi).
Answer: B

q:
Let Q denote a queue containing sixteen numbers and S be an empty stack. Head(Q) returns the element at the head of the queue Q without removing it from Q. Similarly Top(S) returns the element at the top of S without removing it from S. Consider the algorithm given below.
The maximum possible number of iterations of the while loop in the algorithm is ________.
exp:
Algorithm stack mein elements ko non-decreasing (top pe bada) order mein sort karta hai.
Worst case: queue decreasing order mein ho, e.g. 16, 15, ..., 1.
Har naye chhote element ko push karne ke liye stack ke saare bade elements pop hokar queue mein wapas jaate hain aur phir dobara aate hain.
Count karo n elements ke liye: worst case iterations = n² (standard analysis).
n = 16 -> 16² = 256.
Answer: 256

q:
Consider the following context-free grammars:
G1: S → aS | B, B → b | bB
G2: S → aA | bB, A → aA | B | ε, B → bB | ε
Which one of the following pairs of languages is generated by G1 and G2, respectively?
opts: {aᵐbⁿ | m > 0 or n > 0} and {aᵐbⁿ | m > 0 and n > 0}
{aᵐbⁿ | m > 0 and n > 0} and {aᵐbⁿ | m > 0 or n ≥ 0}
{aᵐbⁿ | m ≥ 0 or n > 0} and {aᵐbⁿ | m > 0 and n > 0}
{aᵐbⁿ | m ≥ 0 and n > 0} and {aᵐbⁿ | m > 0 or n > 0}
exp:
G1: S → aS kitni bhi a's (m ≥ 0), phir B → b | bB kam se kam ek b (n > 0). L(G1) = {aᵐbⁿ | m ≥ 0, n > 0}.
G2: S → aA (kam se kam ek a, phir a*b*) ya S → bB (kam se kam ek b, b*).
Toh G2 = aᵐbⁿ jahan string empty nahi: m > 0 or n > 0.
Answer: D

q:
Consider the transition diagram of a PDA given below with input alphabet Σ = {a, b} and stack alphabet Γ = {X, Z}. Z is the initial stack symbol. Let L denote the language accepted by the PDA.
States: q0 (start, final), q1, q2 (final).
q0 → q0 on a, X/XX and a, Z/XZ
q0 → q1 on b, X/ε
q1 → q1 on b, X/ε
q1 → q2 on ε, Z/Z
Which one of the following is TRUE?
opts: L = {aⁿbⁿ | n ≥ 0} and is not accepted by any finite automata
L = {aⁿ | n ≥ 0} ∪ {aⁿbⁿ | n ≥ 0} and is not accepted by any deterministic PDA
L is not accepted by any Turing machine that halts on every input
L = {aⁿ | n ≥ 0} ∪ {aⁿbⁿ | n ≥ 0} and is deterministic context-free
exp:
q0 start aur final dono hai -> aⁿ (n ≥ 0) sab accept (final state acceptance).
q0 mein har a pe X push; b aane par X pop karte hue q1; jab stack pe Z dikhe (a's = b's) to ε-move se q2 (final).
Toh aⁿbⁿ (n ≥ 1) accept.
L = {aⁿ} ∪ {aⁿbⁿ}.
Har configuration mein ek hi move possible hai (ε-move sirf Z top par, jahan koi b-move nahi) -> PDA deterministic hai, L DCFL.
Answer: D

q: Let X be a recursive language and Y be a recursively enumerable but not recursive language. Let W and Z be two languages such that Ȳ reduces to W, and Z reduces to X̄ (reduction means the standard many-one reduction). Which one of the following statements is TRUE?
opts: W can be recursively enumerable and Z is recursive.
W can be recursive and Z is recursively enumerable.
W is not recursively enumerable and Z is recursive.
W is not recursively enumerable and Z is not recursive.
exp:
Y RE hai par recursive nahi -> Ȳ RE nahi hai.
Ȳ ≤ W: agar W RE hota to Ȳ bhi RE hota. Contradiction -> W not RE.
X recursive -> X̄ bhi recursive.
Z ≤ X̄ -> Z bhi recursive (decidability neeche flow karti hai).
Answer: C

q:
The attributes of three arithmetic operators in some programming language are given below.
Operator | Precedence | Associativity | Arity
+        | High       | Left          | Binary
−        | Medium     | Right         | Binary
∗        | Low        | Left          | Binary
The value of the expression 2 − 5 + 1 − 7 ∗ 3 in this language is ________.
exp:
Sabse high precedence '+': 5 + 1 = 6 -> 2 − 6 − 7 ∗ 3.
Phir '−' (medium, right associative): 2 − (6 − 7) = 2 − (−1) = 3.
Sabse last '∗' (low): 3 ∗ 3 = 9.
Poora parse: (2 − ((5 + 1) − 7)) ∗ 3.
Trap: '−' ko left-associative lena -> (2−6)−7 = −11.
Answer: 9

Derivation: S → aA → aSb → aab.
Bottom-up parser reductions reverse rightmost derivation order mein karta hai.
Pehle second 'a' reduce: S → a -> print 2.
Phir Sb reduce: A → Sb -> print 3.
Phir aA reduce: S → aA -> print 1.
Output: 2 3 1.
Answer: C

q: Consider a computer system with 40-bit virtual addressing and page size of sixteen kilobytes. If the computer system has a one-level page table per process and each page table entry requires 48 bits, then the size of the per-process page table is ________ megabytes.
exp:
Page size = 16 KB = 2¹⁴ -> offset 14 bits.
Pages = 2⁴⁰ / 2¹⁴ = 2²⁶ entries.
PTE = 48 bits = 6 bytes.
Page table = 2²⁶ × 6 bytes = 64M × 6 = 384 MB.
Answer: 384

q: Consider a disk queue with requests for I/O to blocks on cylinders 47, 38, 121, 191, 87, 11, 92, 10. The C-LOOK scheduling algorithm is used. The head is initially at cylinder number 63, moving towards larger cylinder numbers on its servicing pass. The cylinders are numbered from 0 to 199. The total head movement (in number of cylinders) incurred while servicing these requests is ________.
exp:
C-LOOK: upar ki taraf serve karo last request tak, phir sabse chhoti request par jump, phir upar.
63 → 87 → 92 → 121 → 191: 191 − 63 = 128.
Jump 191 → 10: 181 (C-LOOK mein return movement bhi count hota hai).
10 → 11 → 38 → 47: 37.
Total = 128 + 181 + 37 = 346.
Answer: 346

q: Consider a computer system with ten physical page frames. The system is provided with an access sequence (a₁, a₂, ..., a₂₀, a₁, a₂, ..., a₂₀), where each aᵢ is a distinct virtual page number. The difference in the number of page faults between the last-in-first-out page replacement policy and the optimal page replacement policy is ________.
exp:
LIFO: a₁..a₁₀ -> 10 faults. a₁₁..a₂₀ har baar last-in page replace -> 10 faults; end mein frames = a₁..a₉, a₂₀.
Second pass: a₁..a₉ hits, a₁₀..a₂₀ = 11 faults. LIFO total = 31.
Optimal: first pass 20 faults (a₁..a₉ ko rakho, 10th frame rotate). End: a₁..a₉, a₂₀.
Second pass: a₁..a₉ hits; a₁₀..a₁₉ faults (dead pages a₁.. replace karo, a₂₀ ko bachao); a₂₀ hit -> 10 faults. Optimal total = 30.
Difference = 31 − 30 = 1.
Answer: 1

q:
Consider the following proposed solution for the critical section problem. There are n processes: P₀ ... Pₙ₋₁. In the code, function pmax returns an integer not smaller than any of its arguments. For all i, t[i] is initialized to zero.
Code for Pᵢ:
Which one of the following is TRUE about the above solution?
opts: At most one process can be in the critical section at any time
The bounded wait condition is satisfied
exp:
Yeh Bakery algorithm jaisa hai, par tie-breaking (process id se) missing hai.
c[j] wait ensure karta hai ki j ka ticket choose ho chuka ho; phir chhote ticket wale ka wait -> mutual exclusion hold karta hai.
Lekin do processes ko same ticket mil sakta hai (dono ek saath pmax padh lein).
t[j] <= t[i] condition se dono ek doosre ka wait karenge forever -> deadlock.
Toh progress aur bounded waiting fail, deadlock possible; sirf mutual exclusion sahi.
Answer: A

q:
Consider the following two phase locking protocol. Suppose a transaction T accesses (for read or write operations), a certain set of objects {O₁, ..., Oₖ}. This is done in the following manner:
Step 1. T acquires exclusive locks to O₁, ..., Oₖ in increasing order of their addresses.
Step 2. The required operations are performed.
Step 3. All locks are released.
This protocol will
exp:
Pehle saare locks lo, phir operations, phir sab release -> growing phase phir shrinking phase = 2PL (actually strict/conservative). -> Serializable.
Locks ek fixed global order (increasing addresses) mein liye jaate hain.
Resource ordering se circular wait impossible -> deadlock-free.
Answer: A

q: Consider that B wants to send a message m that is digitally signed to A. Let the pair of private and public keys for A and B be denoted by Kₓ⁻ and Kₓ⁺ for x = A, B, respectively. Let Kₓ(m) represent the operation of encrypting m with a key Kₓ and H(m) represent the message digest. Which one of the following indicates the CORRECT way of sending the message m along with the digital signature to A?
exp:
Digital signature = sender apni PRIVATE key se message digest encrypt karta hai.
Sender B hai -> K_B⁻(H(m)).
A, B ki public key K_B⁺ se decrypt karke H(m) verify karega.
A ki private key B ke paas hoti hi nahi; public key se sign karna authenticity nahi deta.
Answer: B

q:
An IP datagram of size 1000 bytes arrives at a router. The router has to forward this packet on a link whose MTU (maximum transmission unit) is 100 bytes. Assume that the size of the IP header is 20 bytes.
The number of fragments that the IP datagram will be divided into for transmission is ________.
exp:
Data = 1000 − 20 = 980 bytes.
Har fragment mein max data = 100 − 20 = 80 bytes (80 multiple of 8 hai ✓).
Fragments = ⌈980 / 80⌉ = ⌈12.25⌉ = 13.
Trap: 1000/100 = 10 bolna, header har fragment mein repeat hota hai.
Answer: 13

q: For a host machine that uses the token bucket algorithm for congestion control, the token bucket has a capacity of 1 megabyte and the maximum output rate is 20 megabytes per second. Tokens arrive at a rate to sustain output at a rate of 10 megabytes per second. The token bucket is currently full and the machine needs to send 12 megabytes of data. The minimum time required to transmit the data is ________ seconds.
exp:
Burst phase: bucket full (1 MB), max rate 20 MB/s par bhejo jab tak tokens khatam.
Burst time t: C + ρt = Mt -> 1 + 10t = 20t -> t = 0.1 s. Is dauraan 20 × 0.1 = 2 MB gaya.
Baaki 12 − 2 = 10 MB token rate 10 MB/s par -> 1 s.
Total = 0.1 + 1 = 1.1 s.
Answer: 1.1

q:
A sender uses the Stop-and-Wait ARQ protocol for reliable transmission of frames. Frames are of size 1000 bytes and the transmission rate at the sender is 80 Kbps (1Kbps = 1000 bits/second). Size of an acknowledgement is 100 bytes and the transmission rate at the receiver is 8 Kbps. The one-way propagation delay is 100 milliseconds.
Assuming no frame is lost, the sender throughput is ________ bytes/second.
exp:
Frame transmission = 8000 bits / 80000 bps = 0.1 s.
ACK transmission = 800 bits / 8000 bps = 0.1 s.
Propagation = 2 × 0.1 = 0.2 s.
Ek frame ka total cycle = 0.1 + 0.1 + 0.2 = 0.4 s.
Throughput = 1000 bytes / 0.4 s = 2500 bytes/s.
Trap: ACK transmission time ignore karna.
Answer: 2500
